                                                                                                                    Thus Ti is not a section of K, and the proof is complete.

                                                                                                                    Remark 2.6. We make some comments about the condition in Theorem 2.5 that
                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                    each Ti is not isomorphic to a section of the product j=i Tj . Since the Ti are
                                                                                                                    simple groups, this condition is equivalent to requiring that, for all distinct i, j, the
by 137.205.72.35 on 02/10/26. Re-use and distribution is strictly not permitted, except for Open Access articles.




                                                                                                                    group Ti is not isomorphic to a section of Tj . Deciding precisely when this condition
                                                                                                                    holds was not easy, but in the case where both Ti and Tj are sporadic simple groups
                                                                                                                    (which is the case with the examples in Theorem 1.2), an almost complete answer
                                                                                                                    is given in [12, p. 238], which provides a beautiful diagram showing exactly which
                                                                                                                    sporadic simple groups are involved in this way in other sporadic simple groups.
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                    The only unresolved case in this diagram is whether or not the small Janko group
                                                                                                                    J1 occurs as a section of the Monster M, but it is now known that J1 is not a section
                                                                                                                    of the Monster, see [40, Sec. 5.8] for a discussion. Considering this diagram (and
                                                                                                                    the situation for J1 , M) we see that, for Ti , Tj any distinct pair of sporadic groups
                                                                                                                    occurring in the statement of Theorem 1.2, if Ti is a section of Tj then Ti = T h
                                                                                                                    and Tj = M (which explains the need for two parts in Theorem 1.2(3)).


                                                                                                                    2.2. Totally 2-closed direct products of simple groups
                                                                                                                    By Theorem 2.5, we need to analyze direct products of totally 2-closed simple
                                                                                                                    groups. With this in mind we introduce the following hypothesis and notation.

                                                                                                                    Hypothesis 2.7. Let G = T1 × T2 × · · · × Tr for some r ≥ 1, where each Ti is
                                                                                                                    a ﬁnite nonabelian simple group, and suppose that, for 1 ≤ i ≤ r, Ti is not a
                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                    section of j=i Tj . For 1 ≤ i ≤ r, let πi : G → Ti denote the projection map
                                                                                                                    πi : (t1 , . . . , tr ) → ti , and deﬁne
                                                                                                                                         Ti = {g ∈ G | πj (g) = 1 for all j = i} ∼
                                                                                                                                                                                   = Ti .
                                                                                                                    As mentioned earlier, (see, for example [32, Theorem 4.16(iv)]), {T1 , . . . , Tr } is the
                                                                                                                    complete set of minimal normal subgroups of G.
                                                                                                                        This notation helps avoid possible confusion by distinguishing between the ab-
                                                                                                                    stract group Ti and the simple normal subgroup Ti of G. Note that Hypothesis 2.7
                                                                                                                    holds, by Theorem 2.5, if G is totally 2-closed with F (G) = 1. We extend the ar-
                                                                                                                    gument in the last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.5 to obtain the following
                                                                                                                    characterization of certain subgroups of G.

                                                                                                                    Lemma 2.8. Let G, r be as in Hypothesis 2.7, and let i ≤ r. If H ≤ G has Ti as a
                                                                                                                    section, then H contains Ti .

                                                                                                                    Proof. Suppose that H ≤ G and H has a section Ti , that is to say, there exist
                                                                                                                    L  K ≤ H such that K/L ∼   = Ti . We need to show that Ti ≤ H. Without loss of
                                                                                                                    generality, we may assume that no proper subgroup of K has Ti as a section. Let 1 ≤

                                                                                                                                                            2350004-11
                                    March 13, 2024 14:46 WSPC/1664-3607                                                                                    319-BMS        2350004




                                                                                                                    M. Arezoomand et al.

                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                    j ≤ r with j = i, and let J = K ∩ ( k=j Tk ), the kernel of the restriction πj |K of πj
                                                                                                                    to K. Then πj (L)  πj (K) ≤ Tj and πj (K)/πj (L) ∼     = (K/J)/(LJ/J) ∼    = K/(LJ) ∼  =
                                                                                                                                                                              ∼
                                                                                                                    (K/L)/(LJ/L), a quotient of the simple group K/L = Ti . By Hypothesis 2.7, Ti
                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                    is not a section of k=i Tk , and in particular, Ti is not a section of Tj . Hence
                                                                                                                    πj (K)/πj (L) ∼  Ti . This implies that πj (K) = πj (L), or equivalently, K = LJ.
                                                                                                                                     =
                                                                                                                    Thus Ti ∼ = K/L = (LJ)/L ∼   = J/(L ∩ J), and since Ti is not a section of any proper
by 137.205.72.35 on 02/10/26. Re-use and distribution is strictly not permitted, except for Open Access articles.




                                                                                                                    subgroup of K, we conclude that K = J, that is, πj (K) = 1. Since this holds for
                                                                                                                    each j = i, it follows that K ≤ Ti , and since Ti is a section of K this means that
                                                                                                                    K = Ti . Hence Ti ≤ H.

                                                                                                                        Lemma 2.8 has an important consequence for factorizations of groups satisfying
                                                                                                                    Hypothesis 2.7. The proof uses the notion of a strip. For G = T1 × T2 × · · · × Tr
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                    as in Hypothesis 2.7, a subgroup D is called a strip if D = 1, and for each i ≤ r,
                                                                                                                    either πi (D) = 1 or D ∩ Ker(πi ) = 1. Note that D ∩ Ker(πi ) = 1 if and only if
                                                                                                                    the restriction πi |D of πi to D is an isomorphism from D to πi (D). The support
                                                                                                                    of a strip is the set {i | πi (D) = 1}, and two strips are said to be disjoint if their
                                                                                                                    supports are disjoint. A strip D is full if πi (D) = Ti for all i in the support of D. A
                                                                                                                    subgroup H of a group G with a given direct decomposition G = T1 × T2 × · · · × Tr
                                                                                                                    is called a subdirect subgroup if πi (H) = Ti for each i = 1, . . . , r.
                                                                                                                    Lemma 2.9. Let G be as in Hypothesis 2.7, and such that each Ti admits no
                                                                                                                    nontrivial factorization. If G = HK is a nontrivial factorization, then CoreG (H) =
                                                                                                                    1 and CoreG (K) = 1.

                                                                                                                    Proof. Suppose that G = HK with proper subgroups H, K, and suppose that one
                                                                                                                    of H, K is core-free, say CoreG (H) = 1. By the assumption on the Ti , we must
                                                                                                                    have r ≥ 2. Let i ≤ r. If πi (H) = Ti , then Ti is a quotient of H, and hence
                                                                                                                    by Lemma 2.8, H contains Ti , contradicting the fact that CoreG (H) = 1. Thus
                                                                                                                    πi (H) < Ti . Now, the factorization G = HK implies that Ti = πi (H)πi (K), and
                                                                                                                    since πi (H) < Ti , and by assumption the group Ti has no nontrivial factorization, it
                                                                                                                    follows that πi (K) = Ti . Thus K is a subdirect subgroup of G = T1 ×T2 ×· · ·×Tr . By
                                                                                                                    ‘Scott’s Lemma’ [32, Theorem 4.16(iii)], K is a direct product of pairwise disjoint
                                                                                                                    full strips of G. Since K is a proper subgroup of G, at least one of these strips, say
                                                                                                                    D, has support of size greater than 1. Let i, j be distinct elements of the support
                                                                                                                    of D. By the deﬁnition of a strip, D ∩ Ker(πi ) = 1 and D ∩ Ker(πj ) = 1, and
                                                                                                                    as we noted above, this implies that D ∼     = πi (D) = Ti and   D ∼ = πj (D) = Tj .
                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                    This implies that Ti is a section of Tj , and hence also of k=i Tk , contradicting
                                                                                                                    Hypothesis 2.7.

                                                                                                                        The next proposition assists us to decide which groups satisfying Hypothesis 2.7
                                                                                                                    are in fact totally 2-closed by reducing consideration to transitive (not necessarily
                                                                                                                    faithful) permutation representations.

                                                                                                                        transitive, we have ϕ(G)(2),Ω = ϕ(G).

                                                                                                                    intransitive on Ω1 , and the same argument shows that K is also intransitive on Ω2 .

                                                                                                                    for σ1 ∈ Σ1 , σ2 ∈ Σ2 , x ∈ X.
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                         We claim that the subgroup T1 is also transitive on Σ1 × Σ2 . Choose (σ1 , σ2 ) ∈
                                                                                                                    Σ1 × Σ2 , and let β1 ∈ σ1 , β2 ∈ σ2 . Since X = G(2),Ω , the G-orbit (β1 , β2 )G is equal
                                                                                                                    to the X-orbit (β1 , β2 )X . First, we note that, since X is transitive on Σ1 × Σ2 , the
                                                                                                                    stabilizer Xσ1 is transitive on Σ2 . Now, σ1 is a K-orbit in Ω1 and so Xσ1 = KXβ1 .
                                                                                                                    It follows that the Xβ1 -orbit containing β2 must contain points from each element of
                                                                                                                    Σ2 . On the other hand, (β1 , β2 )G = (β1 , β2 )X implies that the Xβ1 -orbit containing
                                                                                                                    β2 is the same as the Gβ1 -orbit containing β2 , and therefore this Gβ1 -orbit contains
                                                                                                                    points from each element of Σ2 , and hence Gβ1 is transitive on Σ2 . Since Gβ1 < Gσ1 ,
                                                                                                                    also Gσ1 is transitive on Σ2 and hence G is transitive on Σ1 × Σ2 . Since G = T1 × K
                                                                                                                    and K acts trivially on Σ1 × Σ2 , we conclude that T1 is transitive on Σ1 × Σ2 ,
                                                                                                                    proving the claim.
                                                                                                                         Finally, for i = 1, 2, let Si = (T1 )σi . Then since T1 is transitive on Σ1 × Σ2 ,
                                                                                                                    S1 is transitive on Σ2 and hence T1 = S1 S2 , a nontrivial factorization, which is a
                                                                                                                    contradiction to condition (a).

                                                                                                                       For proving that a simple group is totally 2-closed, the following immediate
                                                                                                                    corollary of Proposition 2.10 gives a reduction to consideration of transitive actions.

                                                                                                                    Corollary 2.11. Let T be a ﬁnite nonabelian simple group. Then T is totally
                                                                                                                    2-closed if and only if T admits no nontrivial factorizations and, for each permu-
                                                                                                                    tation representation ϕ : G → Sym(Ω) with |Ω| > 1 and ϕ(G) transitive, we have
                                                                                                                    ϕ(G)(2),Ω = ϕ(G).

                                                                                                                        To summarize this section, we have proved that to determine the ﬁnite totally
                                                                                                                    2-closed groups G with F (G) = 1, we need only consider the groups G which
                                                                                                                    are a direct product of a subset of the nonabelian ﬁnite simple groups listed in

                                                                                                                    Proposition 2.12. Furthermore, the direct factors must satisfy the conditions listed
                                                                                                                    in Theorem 2.5. Finally, by Corollary 2.11, such a group is totally 2-closed if and
                                                                                                                    only if it is 2-closed in each of its (not necessarily faithful) transitive permutation
                                                                                                                    representations. We investigate the transitive representations of these, and other
                                                                                                                    more general, groups in Sec. 3.

                                                                                                                    3. Tools for Analyzing Imprimitive Actions
                                                                                                                    In this section, we introduce some group theoretic and combinatorial tools for study-
                                                                                                                    ing 2-closures of transitive group actions.
                                                                                                                        Let Ω be a ﬁnite set, and let G be a subgroup of Sym(Ω). A partition Σ of Ω
                                                                                                                    is G-invariant if each element of G permutes the parts of Σ among themselves. A
                                                                                                                    partition is said to be trivial either if it consists of a single part, namely, Ω, or if
                                                                                                                    each of its parts consists of a single point. All other partitions are nontrivial. Each
                                                                                                                    transitive permutation group G leaves invariant these two trivial partitions, and G
                                                                                                                    is called primitive if the only G-invariant partitions are the two trivial partitions;
                                                                                                                    otherwise G is said to be imprimitive.
                                                                                                                        Higman’s landmark result [17, (1.12)] in this area (which we will use) is that a
                                                                                                                    ﬁnite transitive permutation group G is primitive if and only if all the nondiagonal
                                                                                                                    G-orbital digraphs are connected.

                                                                                                                    Lemma 3.1. Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be transitive on Ω, and let X = G(2),Ω . Suppose that
                                                                                                                    Σ is a nontrivial G-invariant partition of Ω, and let G = GΣ denote the subgroup
                                                                                                                    of Sym(Σ) induced by G.
                                                                                                                    (a) Then Σ is also X-invariant, and the induced group X = X Σ satisﬁes X ≤
                                                                                                                          (2),Σ
                                                                                                                        G     .

                                                                                                                    X have the same invariant partitions in Ω, so Σ is X-invariant. This implies that ϕ
                                                                                                                    is X-invariant in the sense that, for all α, β ∈ Ω and x ∈ X, ϕ(αx , β x ) = (Bαx , Bβx ).
                                                                                                                    We show that X leaves invariant each G-invariant subset of Σ × Σ: let Δ ⊆ Σ × Σ
                                                                                                                    be G-invariant, and let Δ ⊆ Ω × Ω be the set of all ordered pairs (α, β) such that
                                                                                                                    (Bα , Bβ ) ∈ Δ. Then Δ is the full pre-image of Δ under ϕ, that is, ϕ(Δ ) = Δ, and

                                                                                                                         By Theorem 2.5 and Proposition 2.10, the classiﬁcation of ﬁnite totally 2-closed
                                                                                                                    groups with trivial Fitting subgroup is reduced to the study of nontrivial transitive
                                                                                                                    permutation representations of groups G satisfying Hypothesis 2.7 such that the
                                                                                                                    simple direct factors Ti of G admit no nontrivial factorizations. Although it would be
                                                                                                                    desirable to reduce further to primitive actions, this seems diﬃcult (and perhaps
                                                                                                                    not possible). Loosely speaking, our goal in this section is to prove that if such
                                                                                                                    groups G are 2-closed in all of their primitive permutation representations, then it
                                                                                                                    is ‘likely’ that they are totally 2-closed.
                                                                                                                         More precisely, we will explicitly construct the 2-closure of a ﬁnite group G
                                                                                                                    acting imprimitively on a set Ω, with the property that its induced action on a
                                                                                                                    nontrivial G-invariant partition Σ of Ω is faithful and 2-closed. To state our results,
                                                                                                                    we require some notation.

                                                                                                                        We begin with a straightforward lemma from representation theory.

                                                                                                                    Lemma 3.4. Let G, Σ, M, s be as in Notation 3.3, let p be a prime, and let
                                                                                                                                                V = {(y1 , . . . , ys ) : yi ∈ Fp },
                                                                                                                    be the permutation module for G on Σ over the ﬁeld Fp . Suppose that M is not
                                                                                                                    contained in a proper normal subgroup of G. Then the only 1-dimensional Fp [G]-
                                                                                                                    submodule of V is the trivial submodule {(y, . . . , y) : y ∈ Fp }.

                                                                                                                    Proof. Let U be a 1-dimensional Fp [G]-submodule of V . Then there is an in-
                                                                                                                    jective homomorphism from U to V , that is, the Fp -space HomG (U, V ) of Fp [G]-
                                                                                                                    homomorphisms from U to V is nonzero. Since V is the induced module (1M ) ↑G ,
                                                                                                                    where 1M denotes the trivial Fp [M ]-module, it follows from Frobenius reciprocity
                                                                                                                    [4, Proposition 3.3.1] that HomM (U ↓M , 1M ) is also nonzero. Thus U has a nonzero
                                                                                                                    quotient Fp [M ]-module acted upon trivially by M , and since dim(U ) = 1, it fol-
                                                                                                                    lows that M acts trivially on U . Thus, M is contained in the kernel of the action
                                                                                                                    of G on U . Since M is not contained in a proper normal subgroup of G, we de-
                                                                                                                    duce that G acts trivially on U . It is then an elementary exercise to prove that
                                                                                                                    {(y, . . . , y) : y ∈ Fp } is the only nonzero trivial Fp [G]-submodule of V . This com-
                                                                                                                    pletes the proof.

                                                                                                                    in Notation 3.3. It makes use of Lemma 3.1. Recall in particular the deﬁnition of
                                                                                                                    base groups in Notation 3.3.7.

                                                                                                                    prime, and that M is not contained in a proper normal subgroup of G. Let J consist

                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                    the diagonal subgroup {(x, . . . , x) : x ∈ R} of BR = Rs ∼ = Cps .

                                                                                                                    Proof. Write the cyclic group R ∼       = Cp additively, and let N be the normal subgroup
                                                                                                                    of X from Lemma 3.5. By Lemma 3.5 parts (b) and (c), X = N  G, N is an
                                                                                                                    elementary abelian p-subgroup of BY = BR = Rs = Cps , and by Notation 3.3.10,
                                                                                                                    G∼ = GΣ = L. Thus BR may be viewed as the permutation module V for the G-
                                                                                                                    action on Σ over the ﬁeld Fp , and N as a nonzero G-submodule. Note that V is the
                                                                                                                    induced module 1 ↑G      M , and by assumption M is not contained in a proper normal
                                                                                                                    subgroup of G. Hence, by Lemma 3.4, it suﬃces to prove that |N | = p.
                                                                                                                        Assume to the contrary that |N | ≥ p2 . Then there exists a nontrivial element
                                                                                                                    y = (y1 , . . . , ys ) ∈ N with the property that ye = 0 for some e ≤ s. Since GΣ is
                                                                                                                    transitive, we may assume, without loss of generality, that y1 = 1. Let O be the
                                                                                                                    union of those M -orbits in Σ containing some Δj with j ∈ J. Since M ∩ Mj is the
                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                    setwise stabilizer in M of Δj , the set O has length j∈J |M : M ∩ Mj | ≥ s/2.
                                                                                                                    By Lemma 3.5(c) and the deﬁnition of J, ρ1,i (N ) is a full diagonal subgroup of
                                                                                                                    R×R ∼   = Cp2 , for all i ∈ O. Thus, there exist automorphisms θi ∈ Aut(R) for i ∈ O
                                                                                                                    such that, if z = (z1 , . . . , zs ) ∈ N , then zi = z1θi for all i ∈ O.
                                                                                                                        Since y1 = 0, the number of nonzero entries in y is therefore at least 1 + |O| >
                                                                                                                    s/2, that is, strictly more than half the entries of y are nonzero. On the other hand,
                                                                                                                    since y also contains zero entries, and GΣ is transitive, it follows that, for some
                                                                                                                    g ∈ G, the conjugate y g has ﬁrst entry (y g )1 = 0. Then, since y g ∈ N , it follows
                                                                                                                    from the previous paragraph that (y g )i = 0 for all i ∈ O, that is, strictly more than
                                                                                                                    half the entries of y g are zero. However, since y g is conjugate to y, this implies that
                                                                                                                    strictly more than half the entries of y are zero. This is a contradiction. Hence,
                                                                                                                    |N | = p and the result follows.

                                                                                                                        The next result is our ﬁrst main theorem in this section. In general, and as
                                                                                                                    mentioned in Sec. 1.1, it is a powerful tool for studying 2-closures of those im-
                                                                                                                    primitive permutation groups which induce a faithful action on a set of maximal
                                                                                                                    blocks. For our study of totally 2-closed groups, it will allow to reduce many of our
                                                                                                                    considerations to primitive actions. We summarize some concepts used in the state-
                                                                                                                    ment and proof: For a ﬁnite group E and a positive integer f , a subgroup D ≤ E f
                                                                                                                    is called a diagonal subgroup if D is of the form D = {(e, eθ2 , . . . , eθf ) : e ∈ F }
                                                                                                                    for some subgroup F of E and automorphisms θi of F ; D is called a full diag-
                                                                                                                    onal subgroup if F = E. If f = 2 and D is a subdirect subgroup of E1 × E2 ,
                                                                                                                    for ﬁnite groups E1 , E2 , then by [32, Theorem 4.8] (sometimes called ‘Goursat’s
                                                                                                                    Lemma’), Ki := D ∩ Ker(π3−i )  Ei for i = 1, 2, and there is a well-deﬁned ho-
                                                                                                                    momorphism ϕD : E1 → E2 /K2 with kernel K1 such that D = {(e1 , e2 ) : e1 ∈
                                                                                                                    E1 , e2 ∈ ϕD (e1 )}. In particular D contains K1 × K2 as a normal subgroup and
                                                                                                                    D/(K1 × K2 ) ∼ = E1 /K1 ∼  = E2 /K2 ; and moreover D is a full diagonal subgroup if
                                                                                                                    and only if K1 × K2 = 1.
                                                                                                                        Finally, we will write Ω(2) for the set of ordered pairs of distinct points of a set
                                                                                                                    Ω, and, for a ﬁnite group Y , we will write S(Y ) for the intersection of all nontrivial
                                                                                                                    subnormal subgroups of Y . Note that S(Y ) is nontrivial only if Y has a unique
                                                                                                                    minimal normal subgroup, which is simple.

                                                                                                                    Theorem 3.8. Let G, Ω, Σ, M, R, L, Δ, s, ρi,j , etc. be as in Notation 3.3, and let
                                                                                                                    X := G(2),Ω and Y = XΔ
                                                                                                                                         Δ

                                                                                                                    (a) Then X = N  G with N = X ∩ BY = 1 as in Lemma 3.5, and N is a subdirect
                                                                                                                        subgroup of a base group BA = As for some A  Y (see Notation 3.3.7).

                                                                                                                    Σ, there exists an edge of the form (1, k) for some k > 1. We claim that ρ1,j (N ) is
                                                                                                                    a full diagonal subgroup of A × A, for all j > 1. We prove this claim by induction

                                                                                                                                                                 

                                                                                                                       The next result is needed to prove some important consequences of Theorem 3.8.

                                                                                                                    Lemma 3.9. For i = 1, 2, let Δi be a ﬁnite set and Ei a transitive subgroup of
                                                                                                                    Sym(Δi ). Let Ω = Δ1 × Δ2 , and consider the product action of E1 × E2 on Ω.
                                                                                                                    Suppose that K, a ﬁnite group, acts on Δi with K Δi ≤ Ei , for each i, such that the
                                                                                                                    induced K-action on Ω is faithful. Let Γi be the set of K-orbits in Δi , and let Fi
                                                                                                                    be the (largest) subgroup of Ei ﬁxing setwise each K-orbit in Γi . Then
                                                                                                                                               (E1 × E2 ) ∩ K (1),Ω ≤ F1 × F2 ,
                                                                                                                    and moreover, if K Δi = Fi , for i = 1, 2, then K (1),Ω is a subdirect subgroup of
                                                                                                                    Fi × F2 .

                                                                                                                    Proof. Write Γ1 := {Λ1 , . . . , Λr } and Γ2 := {Π1 , . . . , Πs }. Then the orbits of
                                                                                                                    K Δ1 × K Δ2 in its action on Ω are the sets Λi × Πj , for 1 ≤ i ≤ r, 1 ≤ j ≤ s. Since
                                                                                                                    the 1-closure of a permutation group is the stabilizer of each of its orbits in the
                                                                                                                    associated symmetric group, it follows that (E1 ×E2 )∩(K Δ1 ×K Δ2 )(1),Ω = F1 ×F2 .
                                                                                                                    Then since K Ω ≤ (K Δ1 × K Δ2 )Ω , we deduce that (E1 × E2 ) ∩ K (1),Ω ≤ F1 × F2 .
                                                                                                                    Finally, if K Δi = Fi , for i = 1, 2, then clearly (E1 × E2 ) ∩ K (1),Ω is a subdirect
                                                                                                                    subgroup of F1 × F2 .

                                                                                                                       We now derive a series of consequences of Theorem 3.8. They show that the
                                                                                                                    question of whether or not GΩ is 2-closed often reduces to the same question for

                                                                                                                    assumptions in Notation 3.3, and recall in particular that this includes the assump-
                                                                                                                    tion that G ∼= GΣ = L. The base size of a ﬁnite transitive permutation group L is
                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                    the minimum size of a subset S of points such that i∈S Li = 1.
                                                                                                                        The next result we state is the second main theorem in this section. As men-
                                                                                                                    tioned in Sec. 1.1, it is not only useful for our proof of Theorem 1.2, but it also
                                                                                                                    serves as a general tool for studying 2-closures of imprimitive groups.

                                                                                                                        we have (Mi ∩ Mj )Gαi = Mi .

                                                                                                                    ﬁxes setwise each orbit of M1 ∩ Mj in its induced action on Δ1 × Δj . Since y1 = 0,

                                                                                                                    4. Total 2-Closure of Sporadic Simple Groups
                                                                                                                    A major objective for the remainder of the paper is to determine precisely which
                                                                                                                    sporadic simple groups are totally 2-closed. In the next few sections we will complete

                                                                                                                                                             2350004-26
                                    March 13, 2024 14:46 WSPC/1664-3607                                                                                          319-BMS         2350004




                                                                                                                                                                                                  Totally 2-closed groups


                                                                                                                    the proof that Theorem 1.1 holds if T is a sporadic simple group. In Proposi-
                                                                                                                    tion 2.12(b), we reduced the list of possible candidates to just eleven sporadic
                                                                                                                    groups. In this section, we will eliminate the groups ON, Co2 , Fi23 , HN, B, and we
                                                                                                                    will show that ﬁve of the remaining six groups, namely, J1 , J3 , Ly, Th, M, are
                                                                                                                    totally 2-closed. The remaining group, namely, the fourth Janko group J4 , requires
                                                                                                                    additional eﬀort and will be treated in Sec. 5.
                                                                                                                        Our broad strategy is to apply Theorem 3.10 to the 11 sporadic groups listed

                                                                                                                    in Proposition 2.12(b). To do this, we require detailed information, ﬁrstly, on the
                                                                                                                    greatest common divisors of the orders of the two-point stabilizers in transitive
                                                                                                                    actions of these groups; and secondly, on the base sizes of these transitive actions.
                                                                                                                    Our main technical result is the following proposition.
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com

                                                                                                                    or M. Further, let M be a proper subgroup of T, so that T acts faithfully and
                                                                                                                    transitively by right multiplication on the right coset space [T : M ]. Then

                                                                                                                    (a) Either T [T :M] has base size at most 2, or (T, M ) is as in Table 1, (where the
                                                                                                                        last two subgroups in the J4 -line may possibly have base size 2).

                                                                                                                        of the orders of the stabilizers in M [T :M] of points of [T : M ]\{M }. Then
                                                                                                                        d(T, M ) divides g(T, M ), where g(T, M ) is as in the third column of Table 1.
                                                                                                                        Moreover, if T = J4 and M = 210 : L5 (2), then d(T, M ) ≤ 30.

                                                                                                                    groups T = J1 , J3 , J4 , Ly, Th, and M. Most of these propositions will prove that
                                                                                                                    the relevant group T is totally 2-closed, and also that Proposition 4.1 holds for
                                                                                                                    T , namely, Propositions 4.8, 4.9, 4.13, and 4.17 for J1 , J3 , Ly and Th, respectively.
                                                                                                                    For the monster however, we give the proof of Proposition 4.1 in Proposition 4.10,
                                                                                                                    and prove total 2-closure in Proposition 4.11. For the fourth Janko group J4 , we
                                                                                                                    give the proof of Proposition 4.1 in Proposition 5.6, and prove total 2-closure in
                                                                                                                    Proposition 5.8. Proposition 4.1 will be applied in Sec. 7 where we study the total
                                                                                                                    2-closure of direct products of sporadic simple groups.

                                                                                                                        Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.2 allow us to apply Theorem 3.10 parts (2) and
                                                                                                                    (3) to the relevant sporadic simple groups, to determine whether or not certain
                                                                                                                    of their imprimitive actions are 2-closed. Studying their primitive actions needs
                                                                                                                    a diﬀerent approach, and for this we use the following lemma. Recall that, for a
                                                                                                                    group G acting on a set Ω, we denote by GΩ the subgroup of Sym(Ω) induced by
                                                                                                                    G. Also, we say that permutation groups GΩ1 and H Ω2 on ﬁnite sets Ω1 and Ω2
                                                                                                                    are permutationally isomorphic if there exists a bijection f : Ω1 → Ω2 and a group
                                                                                                                    isomorphism ϕ : GΩ1 → H Ω2 such that f (αg ) = f (α)gϕ for all α ∈ Ω1 , g ∈ GΩ1 .

                                                                                                                    Lemma 4.3. Let T be a ﬁnite simple group with proper subgroup M, and let Ω =
                                                                                                                    [T : M ] so that T ≤ Sym(Ω), acting by right multiplication, and M = Tα for the
                                                                                                                    point α = M ∈ Ω.
                                                                                                                    (a) If also T < G ≤ Aut(T ), and M = T ∩ K for some K ≤ G such that T K = G
                                                                                                                        and G[G:K] has base size 2, then the actions of T on Ω and on [G : K] are
                                                                                                                        permutationally isomorphic, and G[G:K] ≤ T (2),[G:K].
                                                                                                                    (b) Suppose now that M is maximal in T, that T [T :M] is not 2-transitive, and that
                                                                                                                        (T, |T : M |) is not one of the following:
                                                                                                                        • T = M11 , M12 , M23 , M24 , or Alt(9), with |T : M | = 55, 66, 253, 276, or 120,
                                                                                                                          respectively; or
                                                                                                                        • T = G2 (q) with q ≥ 3 a prime power and |T : M | = 12 q 3 (q 3 − 1); or
                                                                                                                                                                                1
                                                                                                                        • T = Ω7 (q) with q a prime power and |T : M | = (2,q−1)   q 3 (q 4 − 1).
                                                                                                                        Then the following hold :
                                                                                                                          (i) if T = Aut(T ), then T = T (2),Ω ;
                                                                                                                         (ii) if M = T ∩ K for any K ≤ Aut(T ) such that K = M, then T = T (2),Ω ;
                                                                                                                        (iii) if, for all K ≤ Aut(T ) such that M = T ∩ K = K, the group (T K)[T K:K]
                                                                                                                              has base size 2, then T = T (2),Ω .

                                                                                                                    Proof. (a) Let M, T, K, G be as in part (a). Since G[G:K] is transitive with base size
                                                                                                                    2, there exists a base {K, Kx} containing the ‘point’ K, for some x ∈ G, and hence

                                                                                                                                                          2350004-28
                                    March 13, 2024 14:46 WSPC/1664-3607                                                                                     319-BMS        2350004




                                                                                                                                                                                        Totally 2-closed groups


                                                                                                                    the stabilizer in G of these two points, namely, K ∩K x , is trivial. Further, since G =
                                                                                                                    T K = KT , we may assume that x ∈ T . The equality G = T K also implies that T is
                                                                                                                    transitive on [G : K] and the stabilizer in T of the ‘point’ K ∈ [G : K] is T ∩K = M .
                                                                                                                    Thus the actions of T on Ω and on [G : K] are permutationally isomorphic. Since
                                                                                                                    M = T ∩ K, we have also M ∩ M x = T ∩ K ∩ (T ∩ K)x = T ∩ K ∩ K x = 1,
                                                                                                                    that is, the stabilizer in M of the point Kx ∈ [G : K] is trivial, so the M -orbit
                                                                                                                    containing Kx has size |M : M ∩ M x | = |M |, while the K-orbit containing Kx has
by 137.205.72.35 on 02/10/26. Re-use and distribution is strictly not permitted, except for Open Access articles.




                                                                                                                    size |K : K ∩ K x | = |K|. Since |K : M | = |T K : T | = |G : T | > 1, it follows that K
                                                                                                                    does not leave invariant the M -orbit containing Kx, and hence G does not leave
                                                                                                                    invariant the 2-relation (K, Kx)T of T . Hence G[G:K] ≤ T (2),[G:K].
                                                                                                                        (b) From now on assume that M is maximal in T , and that T is as in part
                                                                                                                    (b), so T Ω is primitive but not 2-transitive. Then by [26, Theorem 1], the group
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                    T (2),Ω is contained in N := NSym(Ω) (T Ω ). Since T Ω is primitive, N is almost simple
                                                                                                                    with socle T Ω . In particular T Ω ≤ N ≤ Aut(T Ω ), and part (b)(i) follows. If T (2),Ω
                                                                                                                    properly contains T Ω then, taking K = (T (2),Ω )α , we have T (2),Ω = T Ω K since T Ω is
                                                                                                                    transitive, K ≤ Aut(T Ω ) since N has socle T Ω , and M ∼ = M Ω = T Ω ∩K = TαΩ = K.
                                                                                                                    Thus in part (b)(ii) we conclude that T (2),Ω = T .
                                                                                                                        Finally, suppose that the assumptions of part (b)(iii) hold, and that T (2),Ω = T Ω .
                                                                                                                    The previous paragraph shows that K = (T (2),Ω )α satisﬁes K ≤ Aut(T Ω ) and
                                                                                                                    M ∼ = M Ω = T Ω ∩ K = K. Further, since T Ω is transitive we have T (2),Ω = T Ω K,
                                                                                                                    and so, by the assumptions in (b)(iii), T (2),Ω has base size 2. However part (a),
                                                                                                                    applied with G = T (2),Ω , then gives a contradiction.

                                                                                                                       Before proceeding further with the general analysis, we illustrate how to use
                                                                                                                    Lemma 4.3 by proving the following useful corollary.
                                                                                                                    Corollary 4.4. Each primitive permutation group isomorphic to J3 or ON is 2-
                                                                                                                    closed.

                                                                                                                    Proof. Let T be J3 or ON, let M be a maximal subgroup of T , and consider T
                                                                                                                    as a primitive permutation group on Ω = [T : M ] acting by right multiplication.
                                                                                                                    Up to permutational isomorphism, each primitive representation of T arises in this
                                                                                                                    way. We need to prove that T is equal to X := T (2),Ω . By [26, Theorem 1], X is
                                                                                                                    almost simple with socle T . In each case G := Aut(T ) ∼ = T.2, so X is equal to either
                                                                                                                    T or G. Note that T has no 2-transitive representations. If M cannot be written
                                                                                                                    as M = K ∩ T for any K ≤ G with K = M , then X = T by Lemma 4.3(b)(ii).
                                                                                                                    So assume that such a K exists, and note that T K = G. By Lemma!4.3(b)(iii), we
                                                                                                                    may assume further that G has base size larger than 2 in its action on Σ := [G : K].
                                                                                                                    Using [9, Tables 1 and 2], the possibilities are as follows.
                                                                                                                        If G = J3 : 2, then K ∈ {L2 (16) : 4, (3 × M10 ) : 2}. In these cases, we use GAP
                                                                                                                    [35]. If K = L2 (16), then GΣ has rank 7, while T Σ has rank 8. If K = (3 × M10 ) : 2,
                                                                                                                    then GΣ has rank 18, while T Σ has rank 28. Thus, T Σ = T (2),Σ in each case.
                                                                                                                        If G = ON : 2, then K = 4.L3 (4).2.2. Here, we check using GAP [35] that GΣ
                                                                                                                    has rank 34, while T Σ has rank 48. So T Σ = T (2),Σ .

                                    March 13, 2024 14:46 WSPC/1664-3607                                                                                     319-BMS        2350004




                                                                                                                    M. Arezoomand et al.


                                                                                                                        We are now ready to outline our strategy to prove Theorem 1.1. Our analysis
                                                                                                                    uses the notion of the depth G (H) of a proper subgroup H of a ﬁnite group
                                                                                                                    G, namely, the least positive integer such that there exists a subgroup chain
                                                                                                                    H = G < · · · < G1 < G0 = G with Gi maximal in Gi−1 for i = 1, . . . , . The
                                                                                                                    maximum value of G (H) over all proper subgroups H of G is the depth of the
                                                                                                                    trivial subgroup, and this is at most the length of the longest subgroup chain in G
                                                                                                                    but may be smaller. For example, 1 < C2 < C22 < Alt(4) < Sym(4) is a subgroup
by 137.205.72.35 on 02/10/26. Re-use and distribution is strictly not permitted, except for Open Access articles.




                                                                                                                    chain for Sym(4) of maximum length four, while Sym(4) (1) = 3 in view of the chain
                                                                                                                    1 < C3 < Sym(3) < Sym(4).

                                                                                                                    Strategy 4.5. Assume that T is one of the sporadic simple groups in Proposi-
                                                                                                                    tion 2.12(b) so, in particular, T admits no nontrivial factorizations. By Corollary
                   Bull. Math. Sci. 2024.14. Downloaded from www.worldscientific.com




                                                                                                                    2.11, T is totally 2-closed if and only if T [T :H] = T (2),[T :H] for all proper subgroups
                                                                                                                    H of G. It follows from Theorem 2.4 that this holds for H = 1, so we need to
                                                                                                                    consider proper nontrivial subgroups H, and in these cases we note that T [T :H] has
                                                                                                                    base size at least 2.
                                                                                                                        We proceed in a series of steps. At Step we will have remaining a non-
                                                                                                                    empty set S of proper nontrivial subgroups of T to consider, where S1 is the
                                                                                                                    set of all proper nontrivial subgroups of T . Either (a) we complete the analysis at
                                                                                                                    Step by concluding with certainty that T is, or is not, totally 2-closed, or (b)
                                                                                                                    we remove some subgroups from S leaving a set S+1 which, if non-empty, will
                                                                                                                    be considered in Step + 1. In particular, for each , S will have the following
                                                                                                                    property:

                                                                                                                    (∗) If H ∈ S , then T (H) ≥ , and if T (H) = and H < M < T , then T [T :M] =
                                                                                                                        T (2),[T :M] and T [T :M] has base size at least 3.

                                                                                                                    Note that S1 has property (∗) since if T (H) = 1 then H is maximal and the last
                                                                                                                    condition holds vacuously. Also, the process will complete in a ﬁnite number of
                                                                                                                    steps since T is ﬁnite. Finally, we describe what we do in Step (for an arbitrary
                                                                                                                    value of ).

                                                                                                                    Step : For each H ∈ S with T (H) = , we determine T (2),[T :H] . To do this when
                                                                                                                      = 1 (that is, when H is maximal in T ), we use Lemma 4.3 together with some
                                                                                                                    known results about the subdegrees of the primitive almost simple groups. If ≥ 2
                                                                                                                    then T [T :H] is imprimitive, and by property (∗), T [T :M] = T (2),[T :M] for all M such
                                                                                                                    that H < M < T . We can therefore use Theorem 3.10 in our analysis. (This of
                                                                                                                    course is the most diﬃcult part of the procedure.)

                                                                                                                    (1) Thus for each H ∈ S with      T (H) =    , we determine T (2),[T :H] .
                                                                                                                        (a) If T [T :H] < T (2),[T :H] , for some such H, then we conclude that T is not
                                                                                                                            totally 2-closed, and the analysis is completed.
                                                                                                                        (b) Else we have T [T :H] = T (2),[T :H] for every H ∈ S with T (H) = .



                                                                                                                                                            2350004-30
                                    March 13, 2024 14:46 WSPC/1664-3607                                                                                    319-BMS       2350004




                                                                                                                                                                                       Totally 2-closed groups
